docs.title: PaoPao’s DataStore Module (PPDB)
docs.text:
PPDB is a production-oriented DataStore wrapper for Roblox. It exists because raw GetAsync / SetAsync usage does not scale well once a game grows beyond a prototype.

PPDB does not try to hide DataStore. Instead, it provides structure, safety, and predictable behavior around it.

The goal is simple:

  • Make reads cheap
  • Make writes non-blocking
  • Make schema changes survivable
  • Avoid losing data during shutdown

If you have ever thought:

“Why is saving player data this annoying?”

PPDB is designed for that exact problem.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
PPDB follows a cache-first, async-write model.

  • Data is loaded once and cached in memory
  • All reads prefer cache
  • Writes are queued and flushed asynchronously
  • Shutdown triggers a synchronous flush

You should not need to:

  • Call DataStore APIs directly
  • Reimplement retry logic
  • Manually handle server shutdown edge cases

docs.title: Global Shared Cache
docs.text:
Instances that reference the same DataStore name share a single in-memory cache per server.

This avoids redundant GetAsync calls and prevents accidental state divergence inside the same server.

docs.title: Non-blocking Reads and Writes
docs.text:
• Reads return immediately from cache when possible
  • Writes are queued and executed asynchronously
  • Gameplay logic never waits on DataStore I/O

docs.title: Shadow Copy on Write
docs.text:
Before a write occurs, PPDB creates a snapshot of the data.

This prevents race conditions between:

  • ongoing reads
  • concurrent updates
  • asynchronous writes

docs.title: Migration Support
docs.text:
PPDB supports ordered migration functions that run after data is loaded.

This allows:

  • evolving schemas
  • adding/removing fields safely
  • avoiding destructive resets

If a migration fails, the original data remains intact.

docs.title: Lifecycle Events
docs.text:
PPDB exposes signals for key lifecycle moments:

  • OnInit — data loaded and cached
  • OnSave — data updated
  • OnDelete — data removed from cache

These are intended for side-effects and integrations, not core logic.

docs.title: Retry Logic
docs.text:
Transient DataStore failures are expected.

PPDB retries failed operations automatically with delays between attempts. This prevents single-request failures from breaking gameplay flow.

docs.title: Debug Mode
docs.text:
When enabled, debug mode logs:

  • retry attempts
  • migration failures
  • write errors

This is intended for development and staging environments.

docs.title: How It Works (High-Level)
docs.text:
PPDB’s internal flow is intentionally simple:

  1. Request data
  2. Check cache
  3. Load from DataStore if missing
  4. Cache and migrate
  5. Return data
  6. Queue writes asynchronously
graph TD
    A[Request] --> B{Cache Hit?}
    B -- Yes --> C[Return Cached Data]
    B -- No --> D[Load from DataStore]
    D --> E[Cache + Run Migrations]
    E --> C

    C --> F[Modify Data]
    F --> G[Async Write Queue]
    G --> H[Save to DataStore]

docs.title: When PPDB Is a Good Fit
docs.text: PPDB is most useful when you are past the prototype phase and start hitting real DataStore problems.

docs.title: 1. Player Data That Lives for the Entire Session
docs.text:
Typical examples

  • Player stats (level, XP, currency)
  • Inventory / loadouts
  • Progress flags, unlocks

Why PPDB helps

  • Data is loaded once (init) and cached
  • Reads are effectively free after that
  • Writes do not block gameplay
  • Automatic flush on leave / shutdown

This avoids the common anti-pattern of calling GetAsync and SetAsync repeatedly during gameplay.

docs.title: 2. Games With Moderate to High Server Count
docs.text:
If your game runs many servers concurrently, PPDB helps by:

  • Reducing redundant DataStore reads
  • Lowering write frequency via batching
  • Avoiding per-action SetAsync calls

It does not provide strong consistency, but it dramatically reduces accidental abuse of DataStore quotas.

docs.title: 3. Games That Evolve Their Data Schema
docs.text:
If your game:

  • Adds new fields over time
  • Renames fields
  • Changes data structure versions

PPDB’s migration system allows you to:

  • Load old data safely
  • Transform it in memory
  • Save it back in the new shape

No forced wipes, no version spaghetti in gameplay code.

docs.title: 4. Async-Heavy Codebases
docs.text:
PPDB is useful when you want:

  • Clean gameplay logic
  • Minimal callback hell
  • Predictable data lifecycle

You interact with cached tables, not DataStore promises.

docs.title: How PPDB Handles Multiple Servers Accessing the Same Data
docs.text: Short answer: soft coordination, not strict locking.

docs.title: The Reality
docs.text:
Roblox DataStore:

  • Is eventually consistent
  • Has no true cross-server mutex
  • Can overwrite data silently if misused

PPDB embraces this reality instead of pretending it doesn’t exist.

docs.title: What PPDB Does
docs.text:
1. Cache-first design
  2. Each server works primarily on its own cached copy

  3. Reduces read contention immediately

  4. Best-effort soft locking

  5. Uses MemoryStore as a coordination hint
  6. Attempts to reduce simultaneous writes

  7. Not a hard guarantee

  8. Last-write-wins model

  9. If two servers write the same key:

    • The later write overwrites the earlier one

  10. This is intentional and documented

  11. Shadow copy on write

  12. Writes operate on snapshots
  13. Prevents corruption inside a single server
  14. Does not prevent logical conflicts across servers

docs.title: What PPDB Does Not Do
docs.text:
• ❌ No atomic multi-server transactions
  • ❌ No guaranteed mutual exclusion
  • ❌ No automatic conflict resolution

If your game allows:

  • Multiple servers modifying the same player at once

Then you must design higher-level rules, such as:

  • One server owns a player at a time
  • Only write on join/leave
  • Treat cross-server updates as eventual, not immediate

PPDB makes this survivable, not magical.

docs.title: Migration Function Examples
docs.text:
Migration functions are pure transforms:

  • Input: old data table
  • Output: new data table
  • Must not rely on external state

They run in order, every time data is loaded.

docs.title: Example 1: Adding a New Field
docs.text:
function migrateAddGold(data)
    if data.gold == nil then
        data.gold = 0
    end
    return data
end

Use case

  • Introducing a new currency
  • Safe for old and new players

docs.title: Example 2: Renaming a Field
docs.text:
function migrateRenameXP(data)
    if data.xp ~= nil then
        data.experience = data.xp
        data.xp = nil
    end
    return data
end

Use case

  • Cleaning up naming mistakes
  • Avoids breaking old saves

docs.title: Example 3: Structural Change
docs.text:
function migrateInventoryStructure(data)
    if type(data.inventory) == "table" and data.inventory.items == nil then
        data.inventory = {
            items = data.inventory,
            capacity = 50,
        }
    end
    return data
end

Use case

  • Moving from flat arrays to structured objects

docs.title: Example 4: Versioned Migration (Recommended Pattern)
docs.text:
function migrateVersioned(data)
    data._version = data._version or 1

    if data._version < 2 then
        data.gold = data.gold or 0
        data._version = 2
    end

    return data
end

Why this is good

  • Migrations become idempotent
  • Easier to reason about long-term
  • Safer when adding future migrations

docs.title: Migration Rules (Important)
docs.text:
• Always return a table
  • Never mutate external state
  • Expect migrations to run more than once
  • Treat input data as untrusted

A failed migration should not corrupt data — PPDB will keep the original if the migration errors.

docs.text:

docs.title: What PPDB Does Not Guarantee
docs.text:
PPDB is intentionally pragmatic, not magical.

It does not guarantee:

  • strong cross-server consistency
  • atomic multi-key transactions
  • protection against last-write-wins in all cases

docs.title: Notes from Me
docs.text:
Important

  • The API is mostly stable, but not frozen
  • Some changes may occur to improve performance or correctness
  • Bug reports and well-justified pull requests are welcome
  • I use some AI tools to write this documentation (btw)

This project prioritizes correctness and real-world usability over theoretical perfection.

docs.title: PPDB.new(name: string, options?: DBOptions): PPDB
docs.text:
Creates (or attaches to) a DataStore-backed PPDB instance.

  • name — DataStore name
  • options — Optional DBOptions

Notes

  • Instances with the same name share a global in-memory cache.
  • Automatically binds a shutdown handler on first creation.

docs.title: DBOptions.new(): DBOptions
docs.text:
Creates an options object.

Fields

  • debug: boolean — Enables verbose warnings and logs
  • migrations: { (data: table) -> table }[] — Ordered migration functions

docs.title: OnInit: Signal
docs.text:
Fired when a key finishes loading and is cached.

Callback: (key: string, data: table)

docs.title: OnSave: Signal
docs.text:
Fired when a key is set or updated.

Callback: (key: string, data: table)

docs.title: OnDelete: Signal
docs.text:
Fired when a key is removed from cache via leave().

Callback: (key: string)

docs.title: OnInvalidate: Signal
docs.text: Reserved for future cross-server invalidation support.

docs.title: init(key: string, defaultData?: table, callback?: (success: boolean, data: any) -> ()) : any
docs.text:
Initializes and asynchronously loads a key.

Behavior

  • Returns cached data immediately if present
  • If loading is in progress, queues callbacks
  • Runs migrations after load

Returns

  • Cached data if available
  • Otherwise defaultData

docs.title: get(key: string, default?: any, ttl?: number): any
docs.text:
Fetches data from cache or DataStore.

  • ttl — Optional cache TTL in seconds

docs.title: set(key: string, value: table): boolean
docs.text:
Sets and caches a value, scheduling an async write.

  • Adds/updates internal timestamp _t

docs.title: update(key: string, fn: (data: table) -> table): boolean
docs.text:
Atomically updates cached data using a transform function.

  • Receives a deep copy of current data
  • Result replaces cached value if valid

docs.title: increment(key: string, field: string, amount?: number): boolean
docs.text:
Convenience helper to increment numeric fields.

  • Defaults amount to 1
  • Warns if field is non-numeric

docs.title: flushWrites(): ()
docs.text: Schedules async writes for all cached keys.

docs.title: flushWritesSync(): ()
docs.text:
Synchronously writes all cached data.

Intended for shutdown use only.

docs.title: leave(key: string, callback?: (success: boolean) -> ()): ()
docs.text:
Flushes and removes a key from cache.

  • Acquires a soft lock
  • Fires OnDelete

docs.title: cleanCache(ttl?: number): number
docs.text:
Removes expired cache entries.

  • ttl defaults to 3600 seconds
  • Returns number of cleaned entries

docs.title: enableAutoCleanup(interval?: number, ttl?: number): ()
docs.text:
Starts a background cleanup loop.

  • interval defaults to 300 seconds
  • ttl defaults to 3600 seconds

docs.title: export(): table
docs.text: Returns a deep copy of the current cache.

docs.title: import(data: table, overwrite?: boolean): number
docs.text:
Imports key-value pairs into cache.

  • overwrite replaces existing keys
  • Returns number of imported entries

docs.title: waitForKey(key: string, timeout?: number): any?
docs.text:
Blocks until a key is cached or timeout expires.

  • timeout defaults to 10 seconds

docs.title: isLoading(key: string): boolean
docs.text: Returns whether a key is currently loading.

docs.title: Notes on Concurrency
docs.text:
• PPDB uses soft locking via MemoryStore (best-effort)
  • Writes are last-write-wins
  • Strong cross-server consistency is not guaranteed

docs.title: Performance Notes
docs.text:
• Global caching prevents redundant DataStore calls
  • Write queuing reduces DataStore operation frequency
  • Automatic cache expiration manages memory usage
  • Cross-server locking ensures data consistency

docs.title: PPDB Setup Guide
docs.text: PPDB (PaoPao's DataStore Module) is a ModuleScript for Roblox that provides a high-performance, caching-friendly, migration-ready wrapper for DataStores with cross-server synchronization. It must be used server-side (e.g., inside ServerScriptService).

docs.title: Step 1: Get PPDB
docs.text:
You have three options to obtain PPDB:

Roblox Asset Library (Option 1, outdated) GitHub (Option 2) Wally (Option 3)

docs.title: Step 2: Install PPDB (for Option 1 and Option 2)
docs.text:
1. Place the PaoPaoDataStore folder in ServerScriptService or your preferred server-side location.
  2. Require the module in your scripts:
local PPDB = require(game.ServerScriptService.PaoPaoDataStore)
-- Or if you placed it elsewhere:
-- local PPDB = require(game.Workspace.MyModules.PaoPaoDataStore)
